name: Masoor Dal
cuisine: North Indian (pan-Indian everyday red lentil dal; also Bengali and Punjabi dhaba styles)

ingredients.name: Onion (pyaz/kanda)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ small onion, finely chopped (about 2 tbsp)

equipment: Small tadka pan or steel ladle (tadka ladle)
Sieve or a bowl for rinsing the dal
Measuring spoons and a cup (a steel tumbler and a normal teaspoon are fine stand-ins)
Whisk, wooden masher or the back of a spoon, to mash the dal

steps.title: Measure the dal
steps.text: Put 45 g (3 heaped tbsp) split masoor dal in a bowl.
steps.visualCue: Salmon-orange lentils, no stones or husks
steps.videoShot: Dal poured from a spoon into a steel bowl.

steps.title: Rinse the dal
steps.text: Cover with water, swirl with your fingers, drain, and repeat 3 times.
steps.tip: Rinsing removes dust and reduces foam while cooking.
steps.visualCue: Water goes from cloudy to almost clear
steps.videoShot: Fingers swirling dal in cloudy water.

steps.title: Load the cooker
steps.text: Put the dal in the cooker with 300 ml water, ¼ tsp (0.7 g) turmeric and ¼ tsp (1.5 g) salt.
steps.visualCue: Dal sits under about 2 cm of yellow water

steps.title: Cook the dal
steps.text: Close the lid and cook on medium heat for 3 whistles.
steps.tip: Sources vary from 1–2 whistles (Indian Healthy Recipes) to 5–6 (Vegrecipesofindia, Hebbar's for whole dal); split red dal needs the low end.
steps.cameraCheck: The cooker with the weight on

steps.title: Release the pressure
steps.text: Switch off the heat and let the pressure drop naturally.
steps.visualCue: The whistle stops; the lid opens easily

steps.title: Chop the garlic
steps.text: Finely chop 2 small cloves (4 g) garlic.

steps.title: Chop onion and tomato
steps.text: Finely chop 25 g onion and 40 g tomato; slit ½ small green chilli; chop 1 tbsp coriander.
steps.videoShot: Chopped onion and tomato in two small piles.

steps.title: Mash the dal
steps.text: Open the cooker. Whisk or mash the dal until smooth and creamy; add a splash of hot water if too thick.
steps.visualCue: Soft yellow, creamy, no whole lentils, pourable like thick soup

steps.title: Heat the ghee
steps.text: Put the tadka pan on medium heat; add 2 tsp (10 g) ghee.
steps.visualCue: Ghee melts, shimmers and smells nutty

steps.title: Add cumin
steps.visualCue: Seeds sizzle and darken slightly, smell toasty

steps.title: Add chilli and hing
steps.text: Add 1 dried red chilli, broken in half, and 1 pinch hing.
steps.visualCue: Chilli darkens a shade; sharp smell

steps.title: Fry the garlic
steps.tip: Take it off the heat as soon as it turns pale gold; brown garlic tastes bitter.

steps.title: Cook the onion
steps.text: Add the onion and green chilli; cook, stirring.
steps.visualCue: Onion soft and light golden at the edges

steps.title: Cook the tomato
steps.text: Add the tomato and a pinch of salt (from the 1.5 g total); cook until soft.
steps.visualCue: Tomato breaks down to a soft paste; ghee separates at the edges

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Pour the whole tadka into the dal, scraping the pan with a spoon of dal.
steps.visualCue: Hot sizzle; orange ghee swirls on top

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Simmer on low for 2 minutes. Add a splash of water if too thick; taste and adjust salt.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Switch off the heat. Stir in 1 tsp lemon juice and 1 tbsp coriander.
steps.visualCue: Bright green coriander on a yellow-orange dal

reasons: a lentil base gives about 12.5 g protein, about 6.4 g fibre, about 4 mg iron and about 160 µg folate for only about 275 kcal, with no frying and no added sugar. Points off for the saturated fat from ghee (about 6.4 g, 29% of the limit) and moderate sodium (about 620 mg). Restaurant dal tadka often uses 2–3 times the ghee or oil and more salt, with a second tadka (est.).

researchRating.basis: a very well-loved everyday dal, published by almost every Indian recipe site; Tarla Dalal's masoor dal tadka shows 4.9/5 from 8 reviews with about 190,000 views, Cooking and Me's version 5/5 from 3 votes, and Vegrecipesofindia's masoor dal has at least 7 pages of comments. Points off because it is seen as a plain home dish, it is rarely named on restaurant menus, and some vote counts are small.

storage: Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 2 days (est.); freezer up to 1 month (est.). Reheat on the stove with a splash of water, stirring, until bubbling; masoor dal thickens a lot when cold.
leftoverRemix: Masoor dal paratha dough or dal soup. Thin leftover dal with water, add a spoon of cooked rice and a squeeze of lemon for a quick dal soup; or knead 3 tbsp thick leftover dal into whole-wheat flour (about 60 g) with a pinch of ajwain and cook as a stuffed-dough paratha.
burnOff: about 3.9 km of running (275 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 5.5 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 6 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: masoor dal is a pulse outside the common vrat rule set (which allows kuttu, rajgira, singhara or samvat flours), and the recipe uses onion, garlic and table salt.

ekadashi.reason: pulses and grains are avoided on Ekadashi in the common rule set; the recipe also has onion and garlic.

jain.reason: drop onion and garlic (see Jain variant).

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; light (about 275 kcal) with about 12 g protein and 6 g fibre, which suits sehri served with rice or roti; moderate salt (about 620 mg sodium).

jain.reason: onion and garlic are root vegetables; drop both and use a pinch of gluten-free hing (see Jain variant). Tomato and dried ground turmeric are kept; stricter Jain households differ on both (single rule not confirmed here).

vegan.reason: ghee is the only animal product; use 2 tsp (9 g) sunflower or mustard oil instead (see Vegan variant).

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, no meat, so it fits a pescatarian diet.

sattvik.reason: skip the 25 g onion and 4 g garlic (see Sattvik variant).

glutenFree.reason: lentils are gluten-free but most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour; use gluten-free hing or skip it (see Gluten-free variant).

dairyFree.reason: ghee is the only dairy; replace with oil (see Dairy-free variant).
